_comment: Identity mapping: device user ID -> the person, and the accounts the
terminal cannot know. Copy this to directory.json (gitignored), replace
the sample rows, and point ZK_DIRECTORY_FILE at it.
The keys are User IDs — what the terminal shows as 'User ID' when you
enrol someone. The push protocol calls the same value PIN on the wire,
which is why the server's parser still uses that word; it is an identity
number, not a password. (The device does have a per-user password, and
this server deliberately never stores it.)
Build the file from the device's own roster:
python3 server.py --dev
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8081/users/sync?token=$ZK_AUTH_TOKEN'
# wait a poll or two for the terminal to answer
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8081/users?token=$ZK_AUTH_TOKEN'
That gives you the user_id and name of everyone enrolled; add slack and
github by hand. Keys must match the user ID exactly as the device
reports it.
slack is the Slack *user ID* (U0123ABCDEF), not the @handle: IDs survive a
display-name change and are what chat.postMessage wants later. Find one in
Slack under Profile -> More -> Copy member ID.
name is required. slack and github may be omitted or left empty for
someone who has no account; they print as '-'.
Keys starting with _ are skipped by the loader, so this block is safe to
keep as a note to whoever edits the file next.
